Learned APP waives Rule for the respondent State.
3. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

4. sentences.text: At the instance of respondent No.2, FIR came to be filed against the husband and family members, wherein, it is alleged that, the accused persons by hatching conspiracy with each other caused mental and physical harassment to the complainant and demanded dowry.
It is further alleged that, accused No.1 - husband beaten the complainant and accused No.2 demanded dowry in form of house, while accused No.4 threatened to kill the complainant.
In this regard, FIR came to be filed against the accused persons.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that, the allegations levelled against the applicants are nothing, but an abuse of process of law and without any specific instance, they have been arraigned as accused.
He further submitted that there is no iota of evidence against the applicants to even remotely suggest any role whatsoever played by them or to connect them with the alleged offence in question.
The applicant No.2 is mother-in-law, applicant No.3 is sister-in-law and applicant No.4 is brother-in-law.
The complainant wife has completely misused the criminal machinery without any case being made out of cruelty with the narration made in the FIR.

He further submitted that, the dispute arose with regard to marital discord between the husband - wife,
however, all the family members are implicated in the FIR.
Even the allegations levelled against the applicants do not prima facie disclose the involvement of the applicants in the alleged offence.
The allegations are only to cause mental and physical harassment and demanding dowry, except this, no any specific averment is made against the applicants.
Further, the allegations made by the complainant are NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined vague and general in nature.
He further submitted that, the applicants have no any past antecedents.
Except mental and physical harassment, no any specific allegations levelled against the applicants.
Therefore, without disclosing their active involvement in the alleged offence, applicant Nos.2 to 4 have been arraigned as accused in FIR.
In view of the above contentions, Mr. Parmar prays to allow present application and quash the FIR against the applicants, as prayed for, in this application.

7. Learned APP appearing for the respondent-State has opposed the present application and contended that, the applicants have committed an offence by causing mental and physical harassment by demanding dowry and also induced accused No.1 husband to beat the complainant.
Therefore, prima facie involvement of the applicants is established and therefore, present application may not be entertained.

8. Having heard learned counsel for both the sides and going through the allegations levelled against the applicants, it prima facie appears that, the dispute arose between the husband - wife due to marital discord, which is private in nature.
The FIR is filed with an ulterior motive and to pressurize the applicant No.1.

It also reveals that due to marital discord between the husband - wife, however,
all the family members are implicated in the FIR.

Even the allegations levelled against the applicants Mahendrabhai Prabhudasbhai ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142603253/
2 do not prima facie disclose the involvement of the applicants in the alleged offence.

sentences.text: The allegations are only to cause mental and physical harassment, except this, no any specific averment is made against the applicants.
Further, the allegations made by the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined complainant are vague and general in nature.

It also noted that, prior to lodgment of the FIR, in the year 2008, dispute arose between the husband - wife and then, in the year 2011, settlement took place and when she the complainant returned to her matrimonial home, at that time, mother-in-law hurled abusive language and incident took place.
At that point of time, no complaint was lodged.

Even in the present complaint,
no any allegations are levelled except the use of abusive language.
Whatever the allegations of physical and mental cruelty are against the husband, who is not before this Court.
From the record, it appears that, applicant No.4 who is sister-in-law, resides at her matrimonial home and never stayed together, except this, no any allegation is made against applicant No.4.
However, the complainant by keeping grudge, arraigned in- laws in the offence.

It prima facie appears that in absence of any legal evidence in support of the accusation, there is no bar to exercise power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure relying on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of State of Haryana & Ors. Vs. Bhajanlal & Ors., [1992 Suppl. 1 SCC 2020]
and State of Andhra Pradesh Vs. Vangaveeti Nagaih, reported in 2009 (12) SCC 466.

sentences.text:
Considering the allegations levelled in a complaint, case on hand squarely falls in the category of Bhajan Lal (supra), wherein, Hon'ble Supreme Court in para held as under:-
"(7) where as criminal proceedings is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined 9.

In Preeti Gupta and another vs. State of Jharkhand and another [(2010) 7 SCC 667], the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:-
"28.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta and another vs. State of Jharkhand and another [(2010) 7 SCC 667]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a matter of common knowledge that unfortunately matrimonial litigation is rapidly increasing in our country.
All the courts in our country including this court are flooded with matrimonial cases.
This clearly demonstrates discontent and unrest in the family life of a large number of people of the society.

29. The courts are receiving a large number of cases emanating from section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 which reads as under:-
"498-A - Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty - Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such Mahendrabhai Prabhudasbhai ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142603253/
3 woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. In Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. State of U.P, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:-
"19. Coming to the facts of this case, when the contents of the FIR is perused, it is apparent that there are no allegations against Kumari Geeta Mehrotra and Ramji Mehrotra except casual reference of their names who have been included in the FIR but mere casual reference of the names of the family members in a matrimonial dispute without allegation of active involvement in the matter would not justify taking cognizance against them overlooking the fact borne out of experience that there is a tendency to involve the entire family members of the household in the domestic quarrel taking place in a matrimonial dispute specially if it happens soon after the wedding.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. State of U.P, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. It would be relevant at this stage to take note of an apt observation of this Court recorded in the matter of G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held that the High Court should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined litigation which was quashed and set aside.

entities.text: G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
"there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their "young" days in chasing their cases in different courts."

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes.
21.

In yet another case reported in AIR 2003 SC 1386 in the matter of B.S. Joshi &
Ors. vs. State of Haryana & Anr. it was observed that there is no doubt that the object of introducing Chapter XXA containing Section 498A in the Indian Penal Code was to prevent the torture to a woman by her husband or by relatives of her husband.

B.S. Joshi &
Ors. vs. State of Haryana & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 498A was added with a view to punish the husband and his relatives who Mahendrabhai Prabhudasbhai ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142603253/
4 harass or torture the wife to coerce her relatives to satisfy unlawful demands of dowry.

entities.text: Mahendrabhai Prabhudasbhai ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
But if the proceedings are initiated by the wife under Section 498A against the husband and his relatives and subsequently she has settled her disputes with her husband and his relatives and the wife and husband agreed for mutual divorce,
refusal to exercise inherent powers by the High Court would not be proper as it would prevent woman from settling earlier.
Thus for the purpose of securing the ends of justice quashing of FIR becomes necessary, Section 320 Cr.P.C. would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing.
It would however be a different matter depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case whether to exercise or not to exercise such a power."
11. The applicants are facing charge of Section 498-A of IPC.
Therefore, as per the allegations made in the complaint, ingredient of Section 498A is made out.

In this regard, it would be apposite to refer the decisions of the Apex Court in case of Abhishek Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2023 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined INSC 779 / (Criminal Appeal No. 1457 of 2015) and Achin Gupta Vs. State of Haryana & Anr.

entities.text: Abhishek Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2023 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Achin Gupta Vs. State of Haryana & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reported in 2024 INSC 369.
Considering the above principles, it appears that the applicants being in-laws, arraigned as accused with an ulterior motive, which would cause unnecessary harassment to the applicants.
So far allegations under Section 323 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 is concerned, no any assault made by the applicants and therefore, the offence under Section 323 of IPC is not made out.

So far allegations under Section 294(b) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 is concerned, the entire incident has occurred in the private residential house, whereas, under the law, more particularly, as per the provision of Section 294(b) of Indian Penal Code, the incident should have occurred in a public place.

So far as offence under Sections 506(2) of IPC is concerned, the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mohammad Wajid and Anr. v. State of U.P. and Ors., reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 624:
2023 INSC 683, held that:-
"Indian Penal Code, 1860; Section 506 - Before an offence of criminal intimidation is made out, it must be established that the accused had an intention to cause alarm to the complainant.

entities.text: Mohammad Wajid and Anr. v. State of U.P. and Ors., reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 624
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (Para 27)."

In view of the above, it appears that general allegations are made in the FIR and, therefore, no case is made out against applicant Nos.2 to 4.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/932/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined Mahendrabhai Prabhudasbhai ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142603253/
5 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, this Court is of considered view that without any specific instance or evidence, the applicants have been arraigned as accused only with an oblique motive.

This Court is of further view that, if the proceedings are allowed to continue against the applicants, the same will be nothing short of abuse of process of law and travesty of justice and therefore, this is a fit case to exercise inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C for quashing of criminal proceedings.
13.
For the foregoing reasons and observations, present application is allowed.

The impugned complaint being FIR No.11191047210038 of 2021 registered with East Mahila Police Station (East),
Ahmedabad City as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicant Nos.2 to 4 herein.
